description: The chief litigation counsel must approve the company's response strategy to a state attorney general's subpoena concerning alleged misleading product claims, including the privilege treatment, production scope, and protective-order approach, with input from discovery counsel and the client liaison.

shared_context.S1: The state attorney general's subpoena seeks company records concerning product claims made during the past two years.
shared_context.S2: The subpoena response is due in 21 days.
shared_context.S3: The company has preserved its email and messaging data for the business units identified in the subpoena.
shared_context.S4: As part of the firm's standard subpoena-response meeting, Mara asks discovery counsel and the client liaison to report any relevant findings or client instructions before she approves the response plan.
shared_context.S5: The firm's subpoena-response protocol requires each reviewer to formally log any responsive privilege finding, including the document count and privilege-log status, before approval; mentioning a finding orally does not complete that reporting step.

PF1.text: During this morning's privilege review, Elliot identified exactly 26 responsive emails that seek or provide legal advice from outside counsel; he has withheld them from the production set and has not yet circulated his draft privilege log.

PF2.text: In yesterday's audit committee call, Nina received the company's instruction that interview notes from exactly five employees in the internal product-claims investigation should not be produced voluntarily and that the company should seek a protective order before producing those notes; the call minutes have not yet been circulated.

acceptance_conditions: Exactly 26 privileged emails must be withheld from production.
A privilege log must be prepared for the withheld emails.
The company must request a protective order before producing the investigation interview notes.
Exactly five investigation interview notes must be subject to that protective-order request.
The response plan must retain the 21-day subpoena deadline.

content_checks.C2: any('privilege log' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The preserved data alone does not identify any withheld material; PF1 changes the withheld-document count to exactly 26 and requires a privilege-log commitment covering those emails.
The subpoena and preservation record do not establish the client's treatment of investigation materials; PF2 changes the plan to request a protective order covering exactly five interview notes.
